raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview This PR makes the `latency_specialized` decode from #61868 faster for DeepSeek-V4.1 on NVIDIA GPUs. Most of the work is in the decode step's kernels: larger batches now stay on the low-latency paths, more of each step overlaps, and the indexers split their work across the TP ranks. "What changed" below goes through each part. On one GB300 tray with DSpark, the decode step takes 5.9–17.0% less time than on `main` at batch 1 to 32, and AgentX P90 interactivity is 4–26% higher at concurrency 1 to 32, with slightly higher throughput. ![Decode step and AgentX, main against this PR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yaoyaoding/vllm/93d0aafb7e0d32b440d597fa680476b5de27d5f9/pr3_perf.png) Left: three ABBA sets at `0cdfc566`, 12 measurements per arm and batch. Right: AgentX at `0cdfc566`, both arms of each concurrency on one tray. ## Validation This branch includes #63914 (merged into this branch), which keeps the specialized decode's FlashInfer paths on `main`'s FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1; this PR's two further paths on FlashInfer internals follow the same rule. The runs below are from before this branch merged `main`: `main` at `76518259` on that commit's wheel with FlashInfer 0.7.2, against this PR at `0cdfc566`, except compute-sanitizer, which ran at `5ab5ef9e`, the commit before it (`0cdfc566` adds only a start-up requirement, no runtime weight updates, a test option, a comment and documentation). After the merge, on `main`'s wheel at `ed1a7307` with FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1, four GB300: these GPU tests pass at `b7bb822b` (`test_kernels.py`, `test_all_gather.py`, `test_decode_topk.py`, `test_sparse_mla_cute.py`, `test_numerics.py`, `test_layers.py`, `tests/kernels/test_engram.py`, `tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py`; all but `test_kernels.py` ran at `d7fcb755`, which differs only in that file), and a TP4 server with `decode_backend: latency_specialized` starts with the specialized decode on and no fallback warning, and answers a completion and a chat request correctly. FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1's MoE finalize adds the top-k products in a different order at small batches, so `b7bb822b` lets one test's finalize comparison allow FP32's reordering error. ### Correctness | Task | `main` | This PR | | --- | ---: | ---: | | GSM8K, strict match (1,319, c8, real verification) | 0.9742 | 0.9735 | | GPQA-Diamond (198 × 16, c32) | 0.789 | 0.791 | | AIME25 (30 × 16, c32) | 0.983 | 0.985 | | RULER NIAH (`single_2`, `multikey_2`, `multikey_3`; 32K, 128K, 256K; 40 samples each), concurrency 8 | 1.000 in all nine cells (40 of 40 each) | 1.000 in all nine cells (40 of 40 each) | | RULER NIAH, same, concurrency 32 | 1.000 in all nine cells (40 of 40 each) | 1.000 in all nine cells (40 of 40 each) | | GSM8K with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` | | 0.9719, no GPU↔CPU sync reported | | GSM8K with `decode_backend` unset (stock decode) | | 0.9704 | | All-gather stress: CUDA graphs of three back-to-back gathers of different sizes, some with the ranks skewed, replayed 2,000,000 times in a seeded random order on four GPUs; every word encodes its rank, gather and replay, checked on the GPU (`test_all_gather.py` as a module; `--custom-all-gather` replays the same graphs on vLLM's custom all-gather) | custom all-gather: 392 stale words | 0 bad words (6,000,000 gathers) |
Tests ```bash # One SM100-family GPU: the new kernels against FlashInfer, cuBLAS or torch references .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_kernels.py tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_decode_topk.py tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_sparse_mla_cute.py tests/kernels/test_engram.py -v # Four GPUs: the all-gather, AllReduceMHC's LL and two-shot protocols, TP4 numerics .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_all_gather.py tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_numerics.py -v # The all-gather stress run (four GPUs), then the same replays on vLLM's custom all-gather .venv/bin/python -m tests.models.deepseek_v41.nvidia.specialized_decode.test_all_gather --replays 2000000 .venv/bin/python -m tests.models.deepseek_v41.nvidia.specialized_decode.test_all_gather --replays 2000000 --custom-all-gather # Four GB300: five-layer model at TP4 with DSpark, switch on vs off .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_layers.py -v ``` | Check | What it covers | Result | | --- | --- | --- | | Kernel tests | Routed experts against FlashInfer up to 192 rows, eagerly, in graphs and over 500 replays with alternating inputs (bitwise); the front against the stock chain; pinned and wide low-latency MXFP8 GEMMs; the replicated embedding lookup; the metadata graph against eager builds, with slow clamping builders | 299 passed (with `tests/kernels/test_engram.py`), 1 skipped | | Decode top-k (CuTe DSL) | An exact top-k of the BF16 logits against `torch.topk`, k 512 and 2048, 1–64 rows: sampled and direct paths, crowded, constant and rising values, NaN and infinities, a sample that misses the top values, the wide 16-CTA rows, CUDA graphs; block mode against the stock `select_candidate_blocks` | 77 passed | | Sparse MLA (CuTe DSL) | Against an FP32 reference: widths of 1–5 chunks (128 to 640 columns), masked columns, a token with no active column, as many tokens as the GPU holds clusters for, with and without sinks, CUDA graph replay | 33 passed | | All-gather | Against NCCL, bitwise: int32, BF16 and FP32 inputs of 1 pack to the full 4 MiB, growing and shrinking from call to call, one rank late each call; the sentinel word; CUDA graphs of three gathers of different sizes, some with the ranks skewed, replayed in a random order with new contents each replay, 4 GPUs | Passed; the stress run: 0 bad words in 6,000,000 gathers | | `AllReduceMHC` | Shrinking and growing batches in one mailbox with LL only, two-shot only (to 200 rows) and both in turn; the two protocols give the same bits, 4 GPUs | 61 passed (the whole file) | | Numerics, layers (4 GB300) | TP4 collectives through the new paths, including the logits and the row-sharded indexer at 1, 2, 5, 8 and 32 requests through the new all-gather; with the switch on the executor runs, embeds from the replicated table and replays its graphs | Both passed | | compute-sanitizer | memcheck and synccheck over the new kernels' single-GPU tests | memcheck and synccheck: 0 errors each (199 tests: 110 in the two new test files, 89 selected from `test_kernels.py`; at `5ab5ef9e`) | | pre-commit | All hooks | Passes | **CI.** The new test files (the all-gather's among them), the `AllReduceMHC` tests (`test_custom_all_reduce.py -k all_reduce_mhc`) and `test_engram.py` join the nightly 4×B200 DeepSeek-V4.1 step. Three tests need hardware that step does not have, and skip there: `test_pinned_mxfp8_mm` and `test_wide_low_latency_mxfp8_mm` (the tactics are pinned for GB300, SM103) and the layers test (four GB300).
### Performance All runs: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on one GB300 tray (TP4), DSpark (5 draft tokens), Model Runner V2, FULL CUDA graphs for decode. The decode step and AgentX use DSpark's synthetic acceptance (length 3.51, as InferenceX runs AgentX); the accuracy runs above verify for real.
Server command and clients Both arms ran the same command, on `main`'s wheel with either `main`'s or this PR's source: ```bash VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_HTTP_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE=900 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","enable_adaptive_verification":false}' \ --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"use_thp":true}' \ --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":true}' \ --additional-config '{"decode_backend":"latency_specialized"}' \ --compilation-config '{"mode":"VLLM_COMPILE","cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[5,6,12,18,24,30,36,48,60,72,96,120,144,192,240,288,384,480,576,768,1020,1536,2046,3072,4092]}' \ --max-cudagraph-capture-size 4092 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-num-seqs 64 \ --max-model-len 1048576 --language-model-only \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice ``` - Decode step and AgentX: the speculative config adds `"rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.51`. - GSM8K: InferenceX's lm-eval GSM8K (5-shot, temperature 0, all 1,319 questions), 8 requests in flight, one run per cell. - GPQA-Diamond and AIME25: zero-shot through lm-eval, reasoning effort high, temperature 0.6, 16 samples of every question, 32 requests in flight, as for #61868. GPQA-Diamond is InferenceX's task (the last standalone A–D letter, 16,384 output tokens); AIME25 is lm-eval's with DeepSeek-R1's math prompt (65,536 output tokens). - RULER NIAH: lm-eval's RULER generator and scorer for `niah_single_2`, `niah_multikey_2` and `niah_multikey_3` at 32K, 128K and 256K tokens, 40 seeded samples per task and length (upstream lm-eval draws 500), 128 output tokens, thinking off, one run per cell. - AgentX: InferenceX's AgentX scenario (AIPerf, the 393-trace corpus), closed loop at a fixed concurrency for 3,600 s. - Decode step: one server per block. A block runs batch 1 (a 524K-token context), batch 8 and batch 32 (84K–648K tokens a request) twice each. The requests are prefilled one at a time, then sent together for 3,000 tokens each, so they decode from the prefix cache. The step is the client-side window in which every request decodes, divided by its chunk count.
**AgentX.** The InferenceX AgentX trace corpus (393 traces), 3,600 s per concurrency, closed loop, DSpark at the synthetic acceptance length 3.51 as InferenceX runs it, at `0cdfc566`. Both arms of a concurrency ran on the same tray, one after the other (the first arm alternates with the concurrency). Each cell reads `main` → this PR. | Concurrency | P90 interactivity (tok/s/user) | Change | Total tok/s/GPU | Change | TPOT p50 (ms) | TTFT p50 (s) | E2E p50 (s) | Requests | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 817.7 → 852.0 | +4.2% | 7,856 → 8,016 | +2.0% | 1.110 → 1.050 | 0.984 → 0.783 | 2.10 → 1.52 | 341 → 395 | | 4 | 666.3 → 808.7 | +21.4% | 10,336 → 10,477 | +1.4% | 1.110 → 1.040 | 0.434 → 0.431 | 1.13 → 1.09 | 764 → 769 | | 8 | 539.6 → 678.7 | +25.8% | 16,813 → 17,198 | +2.3% | 1.280 → 1.110 | 0.414 → 0.434 | 1.26 → 1.16 | 1,443 → 1,456 | | 16 | 431.1 → 536.2 | +24.4% | 29,316 → 29,922 | +2.1% | 1.520 → 1.230 | 0.496 → 0.448 | 1.30 → 1.11 | 2,715 → 2,748 | | 32 | 225.0 → 258.2 | +14.8% | 61,858 → 63,312 | +2.3% | 2.210 → 1.640 | 0.829 → 0.671 | 2.30 → 1.80 | 4,869 → 4,966 | Some trace turns ask for one output token. When that token ends the reasoning, the response has no content, and the client records the request as an error: 0–1 such requests a run for `main` and 0–1 for this PR.
TTFT: API server and engine AgentX TTFT is mostly the API server's single-threaded work before the engine sees the request: chat-template rendering and tokenization of the whole conversation. aiperf's per-request `request_ack_ns` separates that work from the engine's (acknowledgement to first token). This PR changes only worker-side code, and the engine part stays within 18 ms of `main` at every concurrency; the TTFT differences in the table are in the API server: | Concurrency | API server p50 (s) | Engine p50 (s) | | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 0.693 → 0.479 | 0.267 → 0.249 | | 4 | 0.215 → 0.219 | 0.177 → 0.167 | | 8 | 0.237 → 0.244 | 0.150 → 0.153 | | 16 | 0.284 → 0.239 | 0.158 → 0.162 | | 32 | 0.503 → 0.354 | 0.214 → 0.213 |
**Decode top-k.** `decode_topk` against vLLM's opt-in DeepSelect and the stock path (FP32 upcast + `cooperative_topk`), k = 512, µs per call: Random BF16 logits; "valid" is the share of each row's columns before its end. One GB300, a CUDA graph of 20 back-to-back calls, median of 20 replays. Each cell: `decode_topk` / DeepSelect / stock. With row sharding, a rank selects 12 rows at batch 8 and 48 rows at batch 32 (6 rows a request, over 4 ranks). - Up to 12 rows, `decode_topk` is faster than DeepSelect at every shape but two: 65,536 columns with 1/8 valid (7.3–7.7 against 4.2–4.3 µs), and 1,048,576 columns with 1/8 valid at 12 rows (17.1 against 16.5). - From 24 rows, DeepSelect is faster when 1/8 of the columns are valid (65,536 columns at 48 rows: 17.1 against 4.3 µs) and at 65,536 columns from 48 rows and 524,288 all-valid columns from 48 rows (44.2–44.1 against 46.1–44.7 µs). `decode_topk` stays faster with all 262,144 columns valid (11.8–22.5 against 26.1–26.2 µs). - Above 12 rows, `decode_topk` does not take 1,048,576-column rows, so they use the stock path (81.7–289.3 µs against DeepSelect's 16.6–76.6). - In block mode `decode_topk` is faster at every size (5.9–12.7 against 9.3–80.0 µs). - Against the stock path `decode_topk` is faster at every shape it takes, except 65,536 columns with 1/8 valid (7.3–17.4 against 6.7–12.9 µs; equal at 24 rows).
All shapes | Columns, valid | 1 row | 6 rows | 12 rows | 24 rows | 48 rows | 64 rows | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 65,536, 1/8 | 7.3 / 4.2 / 6.7 | 7.4 / 4.2 / 7.0 | 7.7 / 4.3 / 7.4 | 8.9 / 4.3 / 8.9 | 17.1 / 4.3 / 11.3 | 17.4 / 4.3 / 12.9 | | 65,536, all | 9.0 / 10.8 / 11.5 | 9.3 / 10.7 / 12.2 | 9.4 / 11.0 / 14.1 | 10.3 / 11.0 / 15.7 | 17.9 / 11.0 / 21.4 | 20.2 / 11.0 / 23.3 | | 262,144, 1/8 | 7.4 / 8.2 / 11.1 | 7.9 / 8.2 / 13.2 | 8.0 / 8.2 / 17.0 | 9.9 / 8.3 / 22.3 | 19.3 / 8.3 / 35.9 | 19.6 / 8.4 / 54.6 | | 262,144, all | 9.5 / 25.8 / 14.6 | 11.3 / 25.9 / 18.6 | 10.1 / 26.0 / 29.7 | 11.8 / 26.1 / 34.9 | 20.8 / 26.2 / 62.0 | 22.5 / 26.2 / 80.7 | | 524,288, 1/8 | 8.7 / 11.0 / 11.8 | 9.0 / 11.1 / 17.2 | 9.3 / 10.9 / 23.8 | 15.5 / 11.0 / 36.3 | 28.5 / 11.0 / 81.4 | 35.0 / 11.1 / 102.6 | | 524,288, all | 12.4 / 16.8 / 18.0 | 11.5 / 17.0 / 29.7 | 28.9 / 43.9 / 49.3 | 37.0 / 44.0 / 63.2 | 46.1 / 44.2 / 130.0 | 44.7 / 44.1 / 151.9 | | 1,048,576, 1/8 | 9.4 / 11.8 / 14.3 | 10.1 / 12.0 / 23.9 | 17.1 / 16.5 / 39.4 | – / 16.6 / 81.7 | – / 16.7 / 149.9 | – / 16.8 / 190.7 | | 1,048,576, all | 12.1 / 20.9 / 27.0 | 12.4 / 21.1 / 49.1 | 27.3 / 76.1 / 90.1 | – / 76.2 / 129.9 | – / 76.4 / 246.8 | – / 76.6 / 289.3 | Block mode (the candidate source: top 2,048 blocks of 8 columns; DeepSelect over the block maxima), 1/8 valid, `decode_topk` / DeepSelect: | Columns | 1 row | 6 rows | 12 rows | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 524,288 | 5.9 / 9.3 | 6.2 / 24.5 | 6.3 / 42.7 | | 1,048,576 | 6.3 / 13.3 | 6.5 / 43.6 | 12.7 / 80.0 |
**Memory and start-up.** The replicated embedding table takes 1.32 GB per GPU and the all-gather's mailbox 48 MiB, which the KV cache gives up (106,281,697 → 105,286,588 KV-cache tokens on the tray, −0.9%). Engine start: the engine's init (profile, KV cache, warm-up) took 98.8–103.0 s (`main`) and 98.8–108.9 s (this PR) with warm compile caches, three starts each; a tray's first start, with cold caches, took 680–748 s in either arm. ## Details **Duplicate-work check.** No open PR extends the DeepSeek-V4.1 specialized decode. Related open PRs: - #62633 adds a swap-AB CuTe DSL decode attention to the FlashMLA mega-attention layer. This PR's sparse-MLA kernel replaces the TRTLLM-gen decode of the `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41` backend, which the specialized decode requires. - #62172 lets `cooperative_topk` read BF16 logits, and #57109 adds FlashInfer's sampled `gvr_2` as an opt-in indexer top-k. `decode_topk` serves only this model's decode indexers. It also selects the candidate source's blocks, and it covers the 1M-wide rows on 16 CTAs. The comparison with DeepSelect is above. - #62635 fuses the finalize with the shared-expert add where the fused all-reduce + mHC does not take it. This PR's MoE finalize stays deferred into that fused kernel.
What changed, and what each part saved when it was added Each row was measured against the tree before it, mostly as decode-step ABBA blocks on one tray (batch B = B requests × 6 rows). They were measured one at a time, on a moving base that also held DSpark-draft changes not in this PR, so they do not add up exactly. | Change | Why | Measured when added | | --- | --- | --- | | Pinned CuTe DSL MXFP8 tactics for the attention projections above 8 rows | The autotuner sometimes picked an unclustered `wo_b` tactic (15.3 against 5.9 µs at 48 rows), about 310 µs a step at batch 8, depending on the server start | Batch 8 −7.3% | | The next layer's mHC coefficients on the side stream at every executor step (was up to 48 rows) | They ran inline above 48 rows | Batch 32 −3.9% | | Low-batch routed experts up to 64, then 192 rows: a fused front, a routing-record prefix, the router's padding mask | Above 8 rows the stock FlashInfer chain ran (routing, sort, GEMMs, finalize) | Batch 2 −8.6%, batch 4 −7.0%; 12 cold layers at 80–128 rows 10–13% under FlashInfer | | Low-latency MXFP8 projections up to 48 rows | FlashInfer's block-scaled GEMMs, 13.5 µs for the three projections at 12 rows against 4.3 µs of HBM time | Attention sublayer at batch 2 50.4 → 48.5 µs | | Dense indexers row-sharded from two requests; Engram WKV run ahead; candidate expansion overlapped | Every rank scored every row of the indexers | Batch 2–21 −0.6% to −4.7% (all separated) | | Two-shot all-reduce + mHC from 64 rows, adapted from FlashInfer's MNNVL two-shot all-reduce | Each rank read four contributions per value; the owner now sums them once | Batch 21 −1.0%, batch 28 −0.9%; 192 rows 15.7 → 12.1 µs per call | | The dense indexer planned before the index-key wait | 6.6–7.2 µs of reset, schedule and cast waited for the keys without reading them | About −25 µs a step at batch 2, −50 at batch 8 (profile) | | Embedding from a replicated table into the hyper-connection streams | Sharded lookup + all-reduce + copy | Not measured on its own: it was added in a set of four changes, which together gave batch 4 −1.6% and batch 21 −1.4%. From the work it removes, about −13 µs a step is expected at batch 2 and −23 at batch 32 | | Indexer metadata builds on branches of their own | 13 nodes ran in series on one block-table branch | Draft end → next target −7 to −10 µs | | Decode top-k from BF16 logits (CuTe DSL) | `cooperative_topk` plus the FP32 upcast took 182 µs a step on the slowest rank at batch 8 | Batch 2 −1.5%, batch 8 −1.5% (two trays) | | Sparse MLA up to 8 requests (CuTe DSL): a cluster per token, one CTA per 128 columns, merged over distributed shared memory | TRTLLM-gen's kernel at these shapes | Batch 2 −5.3%, batch 4 −2.7%, batch 8 −4.9% | | GEMM2 starts per token tile | GEMM2 waited for GEMM1's whole grid | MoE pair at batch 2 39.2 → 35.4 µs a layer; batch 2 −1.6%, batch 8 −1.3% | | The front's top-k over eight CTAs; its stores after the cluster release | The top-k was issue-bound on one SM (0.18 µs a row) | Batch 2 −1.1%, batch 4 −1.6% (five sets, three trays) | | Layer 20's top-k on 16 CTAs a row | Its 1M-wide rows fell back to the upcast and the stock top-k | Layer 20 at batch 2 38.5 → 24.7 µs a step; batch 2 −1.1% | | The executor's own all-gather for the indexer rows and the logits (CuTe DSL) | `main` gathers them with the custom all-gather, whose Lamport kernel never waits for the rank's own multicast copy, so a late copy can corrupt a later gather of another size (`test_all_gather.py --custom-all-gather` reproduces it) | Not measured on its own | | The decode Q/KV norm and the fused `wo_a` trigger their dependents early (≤ 48 rows) | `wq_b` and `wo_b` load their weights before their own wait, but were launched late | Attention per layer at batch 2 34.9 → 33.4 µs, about −60 µs a step |

Thanks for the work! One note on the top-k comparison and related work: your benchmark includes the `as_fp32_logits` cast in the top-k measurements. `cooperative_topk` isn’t inherently FP32-only; it’s being extended to read BF16 directly actually (#62172, WIP). It should be worst-case as fast as on FP32 (no `as_fp32_logits` cast), and most likely faster. Just in case this is helpful. 

I see in your table, even with the cast included in the measurements (which adds a big overhead), decode_topk slowing down at 48–64 rows, with cooperative ahead.
stamped for CI

detail.body:
## Overview This PR makes the `latency_specialized` decode from #61868 faster for DeepSeek-V4.1 on NVIDIA GPUs. Most of the work is in the decode step's kernels: larger batches now stay on the low-latency paths, more of each step overlaps, and the indexers split their work across the TP ranks. "What changed" below goes through each part. On one GB300 tray with DSpark, the decode step takes 5.9–17.0% less time than on `main` at batch 1 to 32, and AgentX P90 interactivity is 4–26% higher at concurrency 1 to 32, with slightly higher throughput. ![Decode step and AgentX, main against this PR](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yaoyaoding/vllm/93d0aafb7e0d32b440d597fa680476b5de27d5f9/pr3_perf.png) Left: three ABBA sets at `0cdfc566`, 12 measurements per arm and batch. Right: AgentX at `0cdfc566`, both arms of each concurrency on one tray. ## Validation This branch includes #63914 (merged into this branch), which keeps the specialized decode's FlashInfer paths on `main`'s FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1; this PR's two further paths on FlashInfer internals follow the same rule. The runs below are from before this branch merged `main`: `main` at `76518259` on that commit's wheel with FlashInfer 0.7.2, against this PR at `0cdfc566`, except compute-sanitizer, which ran at `5ab5ef9e`, the commit before it (`0cdfc566` adds only a start-up requirement, no runtime weight updates, a test option, a comment and documentation). After the merge, on `main`'s wheel at `ed1a7307` with FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1, four GB300: these GPU tests pass at `b7bb822b` (`test_kernels.py`, `test_all_gather.py`, `test_decode_topk.py`, `test_sparse_mla_cute.py`, `test_numerics.py`, `test_layers.py`, `tests/kernels/test_engram.py`, `tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py`; all but `test_kernels.py` ran at `d7fcb755`, which differs only in that file), and a TP4 server with `decode_backend: latency_specialized` starts with the specialized decode on and no fallback warning, and answers a completion and a chat request correctly. FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1's MoE finalize adds the top-k products in a different order at small batches, so `b7bb822b` lets one test's finalize comparison allow FP32's reordering error. ### Correctness | Task | `main` | This PR | | --- | ---: | ---: | | GSM8K, strict match (1,319, c8, real verification) | 0.9742 | 0.9735 | | GPQA-Diamond (198 × 16, c32) | 0.789 | 0.791 | | AIME25 (30 × 16, c32) | 0.983 | 0.985 | | RULER NIAH (`single_2`, `multikey_2`, `multikey_3`; 32K, 128K, 256K; 40 samples each), concurrency 8 | 1.000 in all nine cells (40 of 40 each) | 1.000 in all nine cells (40 of 40 each) | | RULER NIAH, same, concurrency 32 | 1.000 in all nine cells (40 of 40 each) | 1.000 in all nine cells (40 of 40 each) | | GSM8K with `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` | | 0.9719, no GPU↔CPU sync reported | | GSM8K with `decode_backend` unset (stock decode) | | 0.9704 | | All-gather stress: CUDA graphs of three back-to-back gathers of different sizes, some with the ranks skewed, replayed 2,000,000 times in a seeded random order on four GPUs; every word encodes its rank, gather and replay, checked on the GPU (`test_all_gather.py` as a module; `--custom-all-gather` replays the same graphs on vLLM's custom all-gather) | custom all-gather: 392 stale words | 0 bad words (6,000,000 gathers) |
Tests ```bash # One SM100-family GPU: the new kernels against FlashInfer, cuBLAS or torch references .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_kernels.py tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_decode_topk.py tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_sparse_mla_cute.py tests/kernels/test_engram.py -v # Four GPUs: the all-gather, AllReduceMHC's LL and two-shot protocols, TP4 numerics .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_all_gather.py tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_numerics.py -v # The all-gather stress run (four GPUs), then the same replays on vLLM's custom all-gather .venv/bin/python -m tests.models.deepseek_v41.nvidia.specialized_decode.test_all_gather --replays 2000000 .venv/bin/python -m tests.models.deepseek_v41.nvidia.specialized_decode.test_all_gather --replays 2000000 --custom-all-gather # Four GB300: five-layer model at TP4 with DSpark, switch on vs off .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/specialized_decode/test_layers.py -v ``` | Check | What it covers | Result | | --- | --- | --- | | Kernel tests | Routed experts against FlashInfer up to 192 rows, eagerly, in graphs and over 500 replays with alternating inputs (bitwise); the front against the stock chain; pinned and wide low-latency MXFP8 GEMMs; the replicated embedding lookup; the metadata graph against eager builds, with slow clamping builders | 299 passed (with `tests/kernels/test_engram.py`), 1 skipped | | Decode top-k (CuTe DSL) | An exact top-k of the BF16 logits against `torch.topk`, k 512 and 2048, 1–64 rows: sampled and direct paths, crowded, constant and rising values, NaN and infinities, a sample that misses the top values, the wide 16-CTA rows, CUDA graphs; block mode against the stock `select_candidate_blocks` | 77 passed | | Sparse MLA (CuTe DSL) | Against an FP32 reference: widths of 1–5 chunks (128 to 640 columns), masked columns, a token with no active column, as many tokens as the GPU holds clusters for, with and without sinks, CUDA graph replay | 33 passed | | All-gather | Against NCCL, bitwise: int32, BF16 and FP32 inputs of 1 pack to the full 4 MiB, growing and shrinking from call to call, one rank late each call; the sentinel word; CUDA graphs of three gathers of different sizes, some with the ranks skewed, replayed in a random order with new contents each replay, 4 GPUs | Passed; the stress run: 0 bad words in 6,000,000 gathers | | `AllReduceMHC` | Shrinking and growing batches in one mailbox with LL only, two-shot only (to 200 rows) and both in turn; the two protocols give the same bits, 4 GPUs | 61 passed (the whole file) | | Numerics, layers (4 GB300) | TP4 collectives through the new paths, including the logits and the row-sharded indexer at 1, 2, 5, 8 and 32 requests through the new all-gather; with the switch on the executor runs, embeds from the replicated table and replays its graphs | Both passed | | compute-sanitizer | memcheck and synccheck over the new kernels' single-GPU tests | memcheck and synccheck: 0 errors each (199 tests: 110 in the two new test files, 89 selected from `test_kernels.py`; at `5ab5ef9e`) | | pre-commit | All hooks | Passes | **CI.** The new test files (the all-gather's among them), the `AllReduceMHC` tests (`test_custom_all_reduce.py -k all_reduce_mhc`) and `test_engram.py` join the nightly 4×B200 DeepSeek-V4.1 step. Three tests need hardware that step does not have, and skip there: `test_pinned_mxfp8_mm` and `test_wide_low_latency_mxfp8_mm` (the tactics are pinned for GB300, SM103) and the layers test (four GB300).
### Performance All runs: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on one GB300 tray (TP4), DSpark (5 draft tokens), Model Runner V2, FULL CUDA graphs for decode. The decode step and AgentX use DSpark's synthetic acceptance (length 3.51, as InferenceX runs AgentX); the accuracy runs above verify for real.
Server command and clients Both arms ran the same command, on `main`'s wheel with either `main`'s or this PR's source: ```bash VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_HTTP_TIMEOUT_KEEP_ALIVE=900 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \ --tensor-parallel-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","enable_adaptive_verification":false}' \ --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"use_thp":true}' \ --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":true}' \ --additional-config '{"decode_backend":"latency_specialized"}' \ --compilation-config '{"mode":"VLLM_COMPILE","cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[5,6,12,18,24,30,36,48,60,72,96,120,144,192,240,288,384,480,576,768,1020,1536,2046,3072,4092]}' \ --max-cudagraph-capture-size 4092 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 --max-num-seqs 64 \ --max-model-len 1048576 --language-model-only \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice ``` - Decode step and AgentX: the speculative config adds `"rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.51`. - GSM8K: InferenceX's lm-eval GSM8K (5-shot, temperature 0, all 1,319 questions), 8 requests in flight, one run per cell. - GPQA-Diamond and AIME25: zero-shot through lm-eval, reasoning effort high, temperature 0.6, 16 samples of every question, 32 requests in flight, as for #61868. GPQA-Diamond is InferenceX's task (the last standalone A–D letter, 16,384 output tokens); AIME25 is lm-eval's with DeepSeek-R1's math prompt (65,536 output tokens). - RULER NIAH: lm-eval's RULER generator and scorer for `niah_single_2`, `niah_multikey_2` and `niah_multikey_3` at 32K, 128K and 256K tokens, 40 seeded samples per task and length (upstream lm-eval draws 500), 128 output tokens, thinking off, one run per cell. - AgentX: InferenceX's AgentX scenario (AIPerf, the 393-trace corpus), closed loop at a fixed concurrency for 3,600 s. - Decode step: one server per block. A block runs batch 1 (a 524K-token context), batch 8 and batch 32 (84K–648K tokens a request) twice each. The requests are prefilled one at a time, then sent together for 3,000 tokens each, so they decode from the prefix cache. The step is the client-side window in which every request decodes, divided by its chunk count.
**AgentX.** The InferenceX AgentX trace corpus (393 traces), 3,600 s per concurrency, closed loop, DSpark at the synthetic acceptance length 3.51 as InferenceX runs it, at `0cdfc566`. Both arms of a concurrency ran on the same tray, one after the other (the first arm alternates with the concurrency). Each cell reads `main` → this PR. | Concurrency | P90 interactivity (tok/s/user) | Change | Total tok/s/GPU | Change | TPOT p50 (ms) | TTFT p50 (s) | E2E p50 (s) | Requests | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 817.7 → 852.0 | +4.2% | 7,856 → 8,016 | +2.0% | 1.110 → 1.050 | 0.984 → 0.783 | 2.10 → 1.52 | 341 → 395 | | 4 | 666.3 → 808.7 | +21.4% | 10,336 → 10,477 | +1.4% | 1.110 → 1.040 | 0.434 → 0.431 | 1.13 → 1.09 | 764 → 769 | | 8 | 539.6 → 678.7 | +25.8% | 16,813 → 17,198 | +2.3% | 1.280 → 1.110 | 0.414 → 0.434 | 1.26 → 1.16 | 1,443 → 1,456 | | 16 | 431.1 → 536.2 | +24.4% | 29,316 → 29,922 | +2.1% | 1.520 → 1.230 | 0.496 → 0.448 | 1.30 → 1.11 | 2,715 → 2,748 | | 32 | 225.0 → 258.2 | +14.8% | 61,858 → 63,312 | +2.3% | 2.210 → 1.640 | 0.829 → 0.671 | 2.30 → 1.80 | 4,869 → 4,966 | Some trace turns ask for one output token. When that token ends the reasoning, the response has no content, and the client records the request as an error: 0–1 such requests a run for `main` and 0–1 for this PR.
TTFT: API server and engine AgentX TTFT is mostly the API server's single-threaded work before the engine sees the request: chat-template rendering and tokenization of the whole conversation. aiperf's per-request `request_ack_ns` separates that work from the engine's (acknowledgement to first token). This PR changes only worker-side code, and the engine part stays within 18 ms of `main` at every concurrency; the TTFT differences in the table are in the API server: | Concurrency | API server p50 (s) | Engine p50 (s) | | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 0.693 → 0.479 | 0.267 → 0.249 | | 4 | 0.215 → 0.219 | 0.177 → 0.167 | | 8 | 0.237 → 0.244 | 0.150 → 0.153 | | 16 | 0.284 → 0.239 | 0.158 → 0.162 | | 32 | 0.503 → 0.354 | 0.214 → 0.213 |
**Decode top-k.** `decode_topk` against vLLM's opt-in DeepSelect and the stock path (FP32 upcast + `cooperative_topk`), k = 512, µs per call: Random BF16 logits; "valid" is the share of each row's columns before its end. One GB300, a CUDA graph of 20 back-to-back calls, median of 20 replays. Each cell: `decode_topk` / DeepSelect / stock. With row sharding, a rank selects 12 rows at batch 8 and 48 rows at batch 32 (6 rows a request, over 4 ranks). - Up to 12 rows, `decode_topk` is faster than DeepSelect at every shape but two: 65,536 columns with 1/8 valid (7.3–7.7 against 4.2–4.3 µs), and 1,048,576 columns with 1/8 valid at 12 rows (17.1 against 16.5). - From 24 rows, DeepSelect is faster when 1/8 of the columns are valid (65,536 columns at 48 rows: 17.1 against 4.3 µs) and at 65,536 columns from 48 rows and 524,288 all-valid columns from 48 rows (44.2–44.1 against 46.1–44.7 µs). `decode_topk` stays faster with all 262,144 columns valid (11.8–22.5 against 26.1–26.2 µs). - Above 12 rows, `decode_topk` does not take 1,048,576-column rows, so they use the stock path (81.7–289.3 µs against DeepSelect's 16.6–76.6). - In block mode `decode_topk` is faster at every size (5.9–12.7 against 9.3–80.0 µs). - Against the stock path `decode_topk` is faster at every shape it takes, except 65,536 columns with 1/8 valid (7.3–17.4 against 6.7–12.9 µs; equal at 24 rows).
All shapes | Columns, valid | 1 row | 6 rows | 12 rows | 24 rows | 48 rows | 64 rows | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 65,536, 1/8 | 7.3 / 4.2 / 6.7 | 7.4 / 4.2 / 7.0 | 7.7 / 4.3 / 7.4 | 8.9 / 4.3 / 8.9 | 17.1 / 4.3 / 11.3 | 17.4 / 4.3 / 12.9 | | 65,536, all | 9.0 / 10.8 / 11.5 | 9.3 / 10.7 / 12.2 | 9.4 / 11.0 / 14.1 | 10.3 / 11.0 / 15.7 | 17.9 / 11.0 / 21.4 | 20.2 / 11.0 / 23.3 | | 262,144, 1/8 | 7.4 / 8.2 / 11.1 | 7.9 / 8.2 / 13.2 | 8.0 / 8.2 / 17.0 | 9.9 / 8.3 / 22.3 | 19.3 / 8.3 / 35.9 | 19.6 / 8.4 / 54.6 | | 262,144, all | 9.5 / 25.8 / 14.6 | 11.3 / 25.9 / 18.6 | 10.1 / 26.0 / 29.7 | 11.8 / 26.1 / 34.9 | 20.8 / 26.2 / 62.0 | 22.5 / 26.2 / 80.7 | | 524,288, 1/8 | 8.7 / 11.0 / 11.8 | 9.0 / 11.1 / 17.2 | 9.3 / 10.9 / 23.8 | 15.5 / 11.0 / 36.3 | 28.5 / 11.0 / 81.4 | 35.0 / 11.1 / 102.6 | | 524,288, all | 12.4 / 16.8 / 18.0 | 11.5 / 17.0 / 29.7 | 28.9 / 43.9 / 49.3 | 37.0 / 44.0 / 63.2 | 46.1 / 44.2 / 130.0 | 44.7 / 44.1 / 151.9 | | 1,048,576, 1/8 | 9.4 / 11.8 / 14.3 | 10.1 / 12.0 / 23.9 | 17.1 / 16.5 / 39.4 | – / 16.6 / 81.7 | – / 16.7 / 149.9 | – / 16.8 / 190.7 | | 1,048,576, all | 12.1 / 20.9 / 27.0 | 12.4 / 21.1 / 49.1 | 27.3 / 76.1 / 90.1 | – / 76.2 / 129.9 | – / 76.4 / 246.8 | – / 76.6 / 289.3 | Block mode (the candidate source: top 2,048 blocks of 8 columns; DeepSelect over the block maxima), 1/8 valid, `decode_topk` / DeepSelect: | Columns | 1 row | 6 rows | 12 rows | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 524,288 | 5.9 / 9.3 | 6.2 / 24.5 | 6.3 / 42.7 | | 1,048,576 | 6.3 / 13.3 | 6.5 / 43.6 | 12.7 / 80.0 |
**Memory and start-up.** The replicated embedding table takes 1.32 GB per GPU and the all-gather's mailbox 48 MiB, which the KV cache gives up (106,281,697 → 105,286,588 KV-cache tokens on the tray, −0.9%). Engine start: the engine's init (profile, KV cache, warm-up) took 98.8–103.0 s (`main`) and 98.8–108.9 s (this PR) with warm compile caches, three starts each; a tray's first start, with cold caches, took 680–748 s in either arm. ## Details **Duplicate-work check.** No open PR extends the DeepSeek-V4.1 specialized decode. Related open PRs: - #62633 adds a swap-AB CuTe DSL decode attention to the FlashMLA mega-attention layer. This PR's sparse-MLA kernel replaces the TRTLLM-gen decode of the `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41` backend, which the specialized decode requires. - #62172 lets `cooperative_topk` read BF16 logits, and #57109 adds FlashInfer's sampled `gvr_2` as an opt-in indexer top-k. `decode_topk` serves only this model's decode indexers. It also selects the candidate source's blocks, and it covers the 1M-wide rows on 16 CTAs. The comparison with DeepSelect is above. - #62635 fuses the finalize with the shared-expert add where the fused all-reduce + mHC does not take it. This PR's MoE finalize stays deferred into that fused kernel.
What changed, and what each part saved when it was added Each row was measured against the tree before it, mostly as decode-step ABBA blocks on one tray (batch B = B requests × 6 rows). They were measured one at a time, on a moving base that also held DSpark-draft changes not in this PR, so they do not add up exactly. | Change | Why | Measured when added | | --- | --- | --- | | Pinned CuTe DSL MXFP8 tactics for the attention projections above 8 rows | The autotuner sometimes picked an unclustered `wo_b` tactic (15.3 against 5.9 µs at 48 rows), about 310 µs a step at batch 8, depending on the server start | Batch 8 −7.3% | | The next layer's mHC coefficients on the side stream at every executor step (was up to 48 rows) | They ran inline above 48 rows | Batch 32 −3.9% | | Low-batch routed experts up to 64, then 192 rows: a fused front, a routing-record prefix, the router's padding mask | Above 8 rows the stock FlashInfer chain ran (routing, sort, GEMMs, finalize) | Batch 2 −8.6%, batch 4 −7.0%; 12 cold layers at 80–128 rows 10–13% under FlashInfer | | Low-latency MXFP8 projections up to 48 rows | FlashInfer's block-scaled GEMMs, 13.5 µs for the three projections at 12 rows against 4.3 µs of HBM time | Attention sublayer at batch 2 50.4 → 48.5 µs | | Dense indexers row-sharded from two requests; Engram WKV run ahead; candidate expansion overlapped | Every rank scored every row of the indexers | Batch 2–21 −0.6% to −4.7% (all separated) | | Two-shot all-reduce + mHC from 64 rows, adapted from FlashInfer's MNNVL two-shot all-reduce | Each rank read four contributions per value; the owner now sums them once | Batch 21 −1.0%, batch 28 −0.9%; 192 rows 15.7 → 12.1 µs per call | | The dense indexer planned before the index-key wait | 6.6–7.2 µs of reset, schedule and cast waited for the keys without reading them | About −25 µs a step at batch 2, −50 at batch 8 (profile) | | Embedding from a replicated table into the hyper-connection streams | Sharded lookup + all-reduce + copy | Not measured on its own: it was added in a set of four changes, which together gave batch 4 −1.6% and batch 21 −1.4%. From the work it removes, about −13 µs a step is expected at batch 2 and −23 at batch 32 | | Indexer metadata builds on branches of their own | 13 nodes ran in series on one block-table branch | Draft end → next target −7 to −10 µs | | Decode top-k from BF16 logits (CuTe DSL) | `cooperative_topk` plus the FP32 upcast took 182 µs a step on the slowest rank at batch 8 | Batch 2 −1.5%, batch 8 −1.5% (two trays) | | Sparse MLA up to 8 requests (CuTe DSL): a cluster per token, one CTA per 128 columns, merged over distributed shared memory | TRTLLM-gen's kernel at these shapes | Batch 2 −5.3%, batch 4 −2.7%, batch 8 −4.9% | | GEMM2 starts per token tile | GEMM2 waited for GEMM1's whole grid | MoE pair at batch 2 39.2 → 35.4 µs a layer; batch 2 −1.6%, batch 8 −1.3% | | The front's top-k over eight CTAs; its stores after the cluster release | The top-k was issue-bound on one SM (0.18 µs a row) | Batch 2 −1.1%, batch 4 −1.6% (five sets, three trays) | | Layer 20's top-k on 16 CTAs a row | Its 1M-wide rows fell back to the upcast and the stock top-k | Layer 20 at batch 2 38.5 → 24.7 µs a step; batch 2 −1.1% | | The executor's own all-gather for the indexer rows and the logits (CuTe DSL) | `main` gathers them with the custom all-gather, whose Lamport kernel never waits for the rank's own multicast copy, so a late copy can corrupt a later gather of another size (`test_all_gather.py --custom-all-gather` reproduces it) | Not measured on its own | | The decode Q/KV norm and the fused `wo_a` trigger their dependents early (≤ 48 rows) | `wq_b` and `wo_b` load their weights before their own wait, but were launched late | Attention per layer at batch 2 34.9 → 33.4 µs, about −60 µs a step |

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""The specialized decode's TP all-gather (``LamportAllGather``) at TP4.
+
+* ``accepts`` by size: 16-byte multiples up to the capacity.
+* Eager gathers of int32, BF16 and FP32 tensors whose sizes grow and shrink
+  from call to call (1 pack to the full capacity), one rank late each call,
+  bitwise against NCCL.
+* The Lamport sentinel word (FP32 negative zero, INT32_MIN) arrives as 0 on
+  every rank, the sending rank included.
+* CUDA graphs of three gathers of different sizes each, some with the ranks
+  skewed, replayed in a seeded random order with new contents every replay;
+  a device-side count of words that differ from the expected concatenation
+  must stay 0. A word left in the mailbox by an earlier call of another size
+  would show up here as a mismatch.
+
+Needs four SM100-family GPUs with NVLink multicast; about a minute. For a
+stress run, run this file as a module
+(``python -m tests.models.deepseek_v41.nvidia.specialized_decode.test_all_gather``)
+with ``--replays 2000000``. With ``--custom-all-gather`` it replays the same
+graphs on vLLM's custom all-gather (``CustomAllreduce.custom_all_gather``, the
+MNNVL Lamport kernel) instead and only counts the mismatched words: that
+kernel never waits for a rank's own multicast copy, and words of an earlier
+call can reach a later one.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import os
+import random
+import tempfile
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+TP = 4
+CAPACITY = 4 << 20  # bytes a rank, as the executor builds it
+REPLAYS = 2000
+LATE_CYCLES = 20_000
+SENTINEL = -(2**31)
+# Pack counts (16 bytes each) of the eager sequence: growing, shrinking, a
+# partial last CTA, one pack and the full capacity.
+EAGER_PACKS = (1, 37, 389, 128, 5000, 3, CAPACITY // 16, 2, 777, 1)
+# Words a rank of each graph's three gathers.
+GRAPH_WORDS = (
+    (4, 2800, 148),
+    (20000, 12, 2048),
+    (512, 8192, 4),
+    (CAPACITY // 4, 4, 64),
+)
+
+
+def _late(rank: int, step: int) -> None:
+    """Delay one rank per step, a different one each step."""
+    if rank == step % TP:
+        torch.cuda._sleep(LATE_CYCLES)
+
+
+def _random_words(generator, words: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Random int32 words, none of them the sentinel."""
+    x = torch.randint(
+        -(2**31),
+        2**31 - 1,
+        (words,),
+        generator=generator,
+        device="cuda",
+        dtype=torch.int64,
+    ).to(torch.int32)
+    return torch.where(x == SENTINEL, 1, x)
+
+
+def _check_accepts(all_gather):
+    assert not all_gather.accepts(torch.empty(0, device="cuda"))
+    assert not all_gather.accepts(torch.empty(2, device="cuda"))  # 8 bytes
+    assert all_gather.accepts(torch.empty(4, device="cuda"))
+    assert all_gather.accepts(torch.empty(CAPACITY // 4, device="cuda"))
+    assert not all_gather.accepts(torch.empty(CAPACITY // 4 + 4, device="cuda"))
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
+        all_gather(torch.empty(2, device="cuda"))
+
+
+def _check_eager(all_gather, rank):
+    from vllm.distributed import get_tp_group
+
+    group = get_tp_group()
+    generator = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(rank)
+    for step, packs in enumerate(EAGER_PACKS):
+        words = _random_words(generator, packs * 4)
+        for dtype in (torch.int32, torch.bfloat16, torch.float32):
+            # One 16-byte pack a row.
+            x = words.view(dtype).view(packs, -1)
+            _late(rank, step)
+            got = all_gather(x)
+            want = group.all_gather(x, 0)
+            assert got.dtype == dtype and got.shape == want.shape, (packs, dtype)
+            assert torch.equal(got.view(torch.int32), want.view(torch.int32)), (
+                packs,
+                dtype,
+            )
+
+
+def _check_sentinel(all_gather, rank):
+    from vllm.distributed import get_tp_group
+
+    generator = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(100 + rank)
+    x = _random_words(generator, 64)
+    x[rank::7] = SENTINEL
+    got = all_gather(x)
+    want = get_tp_group().all_gather(x, 0)
+    want = torch.where(want == SENTINEL, 0, want)
+    assert torch.equal(got, want)
+    negative_zero = torch.full((8,), -0.0, device="cuda")
+    gathered = all_gather(negative_zero)
+    assert torch.equal(gathered.view(torch.int32), torch.zeros_like(gathered).int())
+
+
+def _pattern(rank: int, kind: int, words: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """(rank, kind, index) as int32 bits, never the sentinel; the replay
+    counter goes into bits 20-25."""
+    index = torch.arange(words, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda") & 0xFFFFF
+    return (rank << 28) | (kind << 26) | index
+
+
+def _check_replays(all_gather, rank, replays, stop=True):
+    """Gather graphs replayed in a random order; returns the mismatch count,
+    after the first 1000 replays with a mismatch if ``stop``."""
+    from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import graph_capture
+
+    counter = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    errors = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int64, device="cuda")
+    graphs = []
+    with graph_capture(device=torch.device("cuda")) as context:
+        for sizes in GRAPH_WORDS:
+            mine = [_pattern(rank, k, n) for k, n in enumerate(sizes)]
+            want = [
+                torch.cat([_pattern(r, k, n) for r in range(TP)])
+                for k, n in enumerate(sizes)
+            ]
+            inputs = [torch.empty_like(m) for m in mine]
+            for skew in (False, True):
+
+                def body(mine=mine, want=want, inputs=inputs, skew=skew):
+                    counter.add_(1)
+                    bits = (counter & 0x3F) << 20
+                    outs = []
+                    for kind in range(3):
+                        torch.add(mine[kind], bits, out=inputs[kind])
+                        if skew:
+                            torch.cuda._sleep(LATE_CYCLES * ((rank + kind) % TP))
+                        outs.append(all_gather(inputs[kind]))
+                    for kind in range(3):
+                        errors.add_((outs[kind] != want[kind] + bits).sum())
+
+                body()
+                graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+                with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=context.stream):
+                    body()
+                # The graph keeps raw pointers: keep its tensors alive too.
+                graphs.append((graph, (mine, want, inputs)))
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    assert not stop or errors.item() == 0, "eager warm-up"
+    order = random.Random(1234)
+    for start in range(0, replays, 1000):
+        for _ in range(min(1000, replays - start)):
+            graphs[order.randrange(len(graphs))][0].replay()
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        if stop and errors.item():
+            break
+    return int(errors.item())
+
+
+def _worker(rank: int, port: int, replays: int, skip_path: str, custom: bool) -> None:
+    from tests.utils import init_test_distributed_environment
+    from vllm.config import VllmConfig, set_current_vllm_config
+    from vllm.distributed import cleanup_dist_env_and_memory, get_tp_group
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.nvidia.ops.cute_dsl import LamportAllGather
+
+    torch.accelerator.set_device_index(rank)
+    with set_current_vllm_config(VllmConfig()), torch.inference_mode():
+        init_test_distributed_environment(TP, 1, rank, str(port), local_rank=rank)
+        ca_comm = getattr(get_tp_group().device_communicator, "ca_comm", None)
+        supported = torch.tensor(
+            [int(ca_comm is not None and bool(ca_comm.mnnvl_lamport_ag_multicast_ptr))]
+        )
+        torch.distributed.all_reduce(
+            supported, torch.distributed.ReduceOp.MIN, get_tp_group().cpu_group
+        )
+        if not supported.item():
+            if rank == 0:
+                with open(skip_path, "w") as f:
+                    f.write("no NVLink multicast")
+            cleanup_dist_env_and_memory()
+            return
+        if custom:
+            assert ca_comm is not None
+
+            def all_gather(x):
+                # It takes floating-point inputs only; the int32 words pass
+                # bitwise as FP32.
+                out = ca_comm.custom_all_gather(x.view(torch.float32))
+                assert out is not None, x.nbytes
+                return out.view(x.dtype)
+
+        else:
+            all_gather = LamportAllGather(
+                rank_capacity_bytes=CAPACITY, device=torch.device("cuda", rank)
+            )
+            _check_accepts(all_gather)
+            _check_eager(all_gather, rank)
+            _check_sentinel(all_gather, rank)
+        errors = _check_replays(all_gather, rank, replays, stop=not custom)
+        total = torch.tensor([errors])
+        torch.distributed.all_reduce(total, group=get_tp_group().cpu_group)
+        print(
+            f"rank {rank}: {replays} replays ({3 * replays} gathers) on the "
+            f"{'custom' if custom else 'Lamport'} all-gather, {errors} mismatched "
+            f"words here, {int(total.item())} on all ranks",
+            flush=True,
+        )
+        assert custom or total.item() == 0
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        cleanup_dist_env_and_memory()
+
+
+def run(replays: int, custom: bool = False) -> str | None:
+    """Run the checks on four GPUs (only the replays on the custom all-gather
+    if ``custom``); returns why they were skipped, if so."""
+    from vllm.utils.network_utils import get_open_port
+
+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+        skip_path = os.path.join(tmp, "skipped")
+        torch.multiprocessing.spawn(
+            _worker, args=(get_open_port(), replays, skip_path, custom), nprocs=TP
+        )
+        if os.path.exists(skip_path):
+            with open(skip_path) as f:
+                return f.read()
+    return None
+
+
+@pytest.mark.distributed(num_gpus=4)
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100), reason="needs SM100"
+)
+def test_lamport_all_gather():
+    if torch.accelerator.device_count() < TP:
+        pytest.skip("needs four GPUs")
+    skipped = run(REPLAYS)
+    if skipped:
+        pytest.skip(skipped)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
+    parser.add_argument("--replays", type=int, default=REPLAYS)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--custom-all-gather",
+        action="store_true",
+        help="replay the graphs on vLLM's custom all-gather and count mismatches",
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    skipped = run(args.replays, args.custom_all_gather)
+    print(f"skipped: {skipped}" if skipped else "done")

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""``decode_topk`` (``decode_topk_cute.py``) against ``torch.topk``.
+
+Token mode: each row's output must be an exact top-k of its BF16 logits in
+the kernel's key order (every index whose key exceeds the k-th largest key,
+then indices whose key equals it), or ``0 .. n-1`` and -1 for rows of at most
+k values. Rows cover the sampled path, short rows (the direct path), crowded
+and constant values, values rising toward the row's end (survivors in the last
+CTA), NaN and infinities, the forced direct path, and a sample that misses the
+row's top values. Block mode must
+select an exact top-k of the 8-token block maxima, as the stock
+``select_candidate_blocks`` on the upcast logits does, with the newest block
+pinned and -inf blocks written as -1.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.nvidia.specialized_decode.attention.decode_topk_cute import (  # noqa: E501
+    SAMPLES,
+    _resident_clusters,
+    cluster_for,
+    decode_topk,
+    supports_decode_topk,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not (
+        current_platform.is_cuda() and current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100)
+    ),
+    reason="needs an SM100-family GPU",
+)
+
+DEVICE = "cuda"
+WIDTH = 262144
+
+
+def order_keys(values: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """The kernel's order-preserving key of each BF16 value, as int32."""
+    bits = values.view(torch.int16).int() & 0xFFFF
+    return torch.where(bits >= 0x8000, bits ^ 0xFFFF, bits ^ 0x8000)
+
+
+def make_logits(rows: int, kind: str, seed: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """[rows, WIDTH] BF16 logits of one distribution."""
+    g = torch.Generator(device=DEVICE).manual_seed(seed)
+    x = torch.randn(rows, WIDTH, device=DEVICE, generator=g)
+    if kind == "crowded":  # few distinct values: long exact ties
+        x = torch.randint(0, 6, (rows, WIDTH), device=DEVICE, generator=g).float()
+    elif kind == "constant":
+        x = torch.full((rows, WIDTH), 3.0, device=DEVICE)
+    elif kind == "rising":  # the largest values at the row's end
+        x = x * 0.1 + torch.linspace(0, 8, WIDTH, device=DEVICE)
+    elif kind == "special":
+        x[:, 7] = float("nan")
+        x[:, 1000::977] = float("inf")
+        x[:, 2000::991] = float("-inf")
+    return x.bfloat16()
+
+
+def check_tokens(logits: torch.Tensor, lengths: list[int], out: torch.Tensor, k: int):
+    """Assert each row's output is an exact top-k (module docstring)."""
+    for r, n in enumerate(lengths):
+        got = out[r]
+        if n <= k:
+            want = torch.arange(k, device=DEVICE, dtype=torch.int32)
+            want[n:] = -1
+            assert torch.equal(got, want), f"row {r} (n {n})"
+            continue
+        assert int((got < 0).sum()) == 0 and int(got.max()) < n, (
+            f"row {r}: ids out of range"
+        )
+        assert got.unique().numel() == k, f"row {r}: repeated ids"
+        keys = order_keys(logits[r, :n])
+        kth = keys.topk(k).values[-1]
+        chosen = keys[got.long()]
+        assert int((chosen < kth).sum()) == 0, f"row {r}: a key below the k-th"
+        assert int((chosen > kth).sum()) == int((keys > kth).sum()), (
+            f"row {r}: missed a key above"
+        )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("kind", ["normal", "crowded", "constant", "rising", "special"])
+# One row, 8 CTAs a row (12), 4 CTAs a row (20), the most rows (64).
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rows", [1, 12, 20, 64])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(("k", "fallback"), [(512, False), (2048, False), (2048, True)])
+def test_token_topk(kind, rows, k, fallback):
+    lengths_all = [
+        WIDTH,
+        0,
+        k - 1,
+        k,
+        k + 1,
+        5000,
+        8192,
+        8193,
+        30000,
+        162000,
+        99991,
+        250000,
+    ]
+    lengths = [lengths_all[(r * 5) % len(lengths_all)] for r in range(rows)]
+    logits = make_logits(rows, kind, rows * 31 + k)
+    assert supports_decode_topk(logits, rows, k, block_mode=False)
+    ends = torch.tensor(lengths, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    out = torch.full((rows, k), 7, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    decode_topk(logits, ends, out, block_mode=False, fallback=fallback)
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    check_tokens(logits, lengths, out, k)
+
+
+def test_token_topk_strided_output_and_graph():
+    """A wider output buffer (row stride > k) and a CUDA graph replay on new
+    logits."""
+    rows, k = 12, 512
+    lengths = [162000, 140000, 600, 9000] * 3
+    logits = make_logits(rows, "normal", 1)
+    ends = torch.tensor(lengths, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    buffer = torch.full((rows, k + 64), 7, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    out = buffer[:, :k]
+    decode_topk(logits, ends, out, block_mode=False)
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    check_tokens(logits, lengths, out, k)
+    assert torch.all(buffer[:, k:] == 7)
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        decode_topk(logits, ends, out, block_mode=False)
+    logits.copy_(make_logits(rows, "rising", 2))
+    graph.replay()
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    check_tokens(logits, lengths, out, k)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "rows,wide,cluster",
+    [(4, 2 * WIDTH, 8), (20, 2 * WIDTH, 8), (4, 4 * WIDTH, 16), (12, 4 * WIDTH, 16)],
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("fallback", [False, True])
+def test_wide_rows(rows, wide, cluster, fallback):
+    """Rows of up to 524,288 logits (the ratio-2 layers' width at a 1M
+    context), which only 8 CTAs a row hold, and of up to 1,048,576 (the
+    candidate source's), which take 16; at 20 and 12 rows more clusters than
+    a GB300 runs at once, so they run in waves."""
+    lengths = [
+        [wide, wide * 3 // 4 + 1, wide // 2 + 1, 9000][r % 4] for r in range(rows)
+    ]
+    g = torch.Generator(device=DEVICE).manual_seed(11)
+    logits = (torch.randn(rows, wide, device=DEVICE, generator=g) - 1.5).bfloat16()
+    assert supports_decode_topk(logits, rows, 512, block_mode=False)
+    assert supports_decode_topk(logits, rows, 2048, block_mode=True)
+    assert cluster_for(rows, wide, torch.accelerator.current_device_index()) == cluster
+    ends = torch.tensor(lengths, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    out = torch.full((rows, 512), 7, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    decode_topk(logits, ends, out, block_mode=False, fallback=fallback)
+    blocks = torch.full((rows, 2048), 7, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    decode_topk(logits, ends, blocks, block_mode=True)
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    check_tokens(logits, lengths, out, 512)
+    for r, end in enumerate(lengths):
+        nblocks = (end + 7) // 8
+        if nblocks <= 2048:  # every block, in order (no -inf blocks here)
+            want = torch.arange(2048, device=DEVICE, dtype=torch.int32)
+            want[nblocks:] = -1
+            assert torch.equal(blocks[r], want), f"row {r}"
+            continue
+        keys = block_keys(logits[r], end)
+        best = keys.topk(2048).values.sort().values
+        assert torch.equal(selected_keys(blocks[r], keys), best), f"row {r}"
+
+
+def test_candidate_source_waves():
+    """Rows that need 16 CTAs are taken for at most two waves of clusters."""
+    waves = 2 * _resident_clusters(torch.accelerator.current_device_index(), 16)
+    logits = torch.empty(waves + 1, 4 * WIDTH, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=DEVICE)
+    for block_mode, k in ((False, 512), (True, 2048)):
+        assert supports_decode_topk(logits, waves, k, block_mode)
+        assert not supports_decode_topk(logits, waves + 1, k, block_mode)
+    narrow = logits[:, : 2 * WIDTH]  # 8 CTAs a row: up to 64 rows
+    assert supports_decode_topk(narrow, waves + 1, 512, block_mode=False)
+
+
+def test_token_topk_sampler_miss():
+    """Large values only at the sampled positions: the sampled cutoff keeps
+    fewer than k keys, so the kernel must recover through the direct path."""
+    rows, k, n = 2, 512, WIDTH
+    cluster = cluster_for(rows, WIDTH, torch.accelerator.current_device_index())
+    per_cta = SAMPLES // cluster
+    chunk = ((n + cluster - 1) // cluster + 7) // 8 * 8
+    positions = []
+    for c in range(cluster):
+        length = min(n - c * chunk, chunk)
+        valid = per_cta * length // chunk
+        positions += [
+            c * chunk + (2 * t + 1) * length // (2 * valid) for t in range(valid)
+        ]
+    x = torch.full((rows, WIDTH), -1.0, device=DEVICE)
+    g = torch.Generator(device=DEVICE).manual_seed(7)
+    x[:, positions] = torch.randn(rows, len(positions), device=DEVICE, generator=g) + 10
+    logits = x.bfloat16()
+    ends = torch.tensor([n] * rows, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    out = torch.full((rows, k), 7, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    decode_topk(logits, ends, out, block_mode=False)
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    check_tokens(logits, [n] * rows, out, k)
+
+
+NEG_INF_KEY = 0x007F
+
+
+def block_keys(logits: torch.Tensor, end: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Keys of a row's valid 8-token block maxima, the newest pinned at +inf."""
+    nblocks = (end + 7) // 8
+    padded = torch.full((nblocks * 8,), float("-inf"), device=DEVICE)
+    padded[:end] = logits[:end].float()
+    scores = padded.view(nblocks, 8).amax(dim=1)
+    scores[nblocks - 1] = float("inf")
+    return order_keys(scores.bfloat16())
+
+
+def selected_keys(ids: torch.Tensor, keys: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Sorted keys of a candidate row's selected blocks, -1 slots as -inf."""
+    assert int(ids.max()) < keys.numel()
+    valid = ids[ids >= 0]
+    assert valid.unique().numel() == valid.numel(), "repeated ids"
+    chosen = torch.full_like(ids, NEG_INF_KEY)
+    chosen[ids >= 0] = keys[valid.long()]
+    return chosen.sort().values
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rows", [3, 12, 20])

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+"""``sparse_mla_decode`` (``sparse_mla_cute.py``) against an FP32 reference.
+
+Each token attends to its own columns: the first 128 index the sliding-window
+pool and the rest the compressed pool, as storage offsets. The cases cover the
+widths of 1 to 5 chunks (128, a partial second chunk, 384, 512, 640), masked
+columns (-1 and columns past a token's length, including a token with no active
+column, whose output is zero), batches from one token to the most the kernel
+takes, sinks and none, and scales other than one. The tolerance allows for the
+probabilities' FP8 rounding (TRTLLM-gen's own error is of the same size).
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.nvidia.specialized_decode.attention.sparse_mla_cute import (  # noqa: E501
+    _max_tokens,
+    sparse_mla_decode,
+    supports_sparse_mla_cute,
+)
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not (
+        current_platform.is_cuda() and current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100)
+    ),
+    reason="needs an SM100-family GPU",
+)
+
+DEVICE = "cuda"
+H, D, SWA = 16, 512, 128
+SWA_ROWS, COMP_ROWS, PAGE = 1024, 8192, 64
+
+
+def fp8(shape: tuple[int, ...], std: float, g: torch.Generator) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Normal values of standard deviation ``std`` as FP8 E4M3."""
+    return (torch.randn(shape, device=DEVICE, generator=g) * std).to(
+        torch.float8_e4m3fn
+    )
+
+
+def make_case(tokens: int, width: int, seed: int) -> dict:
+    """Pools, indices with masked columns, and lengths for ``tokens`` tokens."""
+    g = torch.Generator(device=DEVICE).manual_seed(seed)
+    swa_pool = fp8((SWA_ROWS // PAGE, PAGE, D), 1.0, g)
+    comp_pool = fp8((COMP_ROWS // PAGE, PAGE, D), 1.0, g)
+    swa = torch.randint(
+        0, SWA_ROWS, (tokens, min(width, SWA)), device=DEVICE, generator=g
+    )
+    columns = [swa]
+    if width > SWA:
+        columns.append(
+            torch.randint(
+                0, COMP_ROWS, (tokens, width - SWA), device=DEVICE, generator=g
+            )
+        )
+    indices = torch.cat(columns, dim=1).to(torch.int32)
+    drop = torch.rand(indices.shape, device=DEVICE, generator=g) < 0.05
+    indices[drop] = -1
+    lens = torch.full((tokens,), width, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    if tokens > 1:
+        lens[1] = max(width - 77, 1)  # a partial last chunk
+    if tokens > 2:
+        lens[2] = 0  # no active column
+    return dict(
+        q=fp8((tokens, H, D), 0.5, g),
+        swa_pool=swa_pool,
+        comp_pool=comp_pool,
+        indices=indices,
+        lens=lens,
+        sinks=torch.randn(H, device=DEVICE, generator=g),
+    )
+
+
+def reference(
+    c: dict, bmm1_scale: float, bmm2_scale: float, sinks: torch.Tensor | None
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """FP32 sparse attention over each token's active columns (K = V)."""
+    swa = c["swa_pool"].reshape(-1, D).float()
+    comp = c["comp_pool"].reshape(-1, D).float()
+    q = c["q"].float()
+    out = torch.zeros(q.shape, device=DEVICE)
+    for t in range(q.shape[0]):
+        n = int(c["lens"][t])
+        idx = c["indices"][t, :n].long()
+        cols = torch.arange(n, device=DEVICE)
+        keep = idx >= 0
+        if not bool(keep.any()):
+            continue
+        rows = torch.where(
+            (cols < SWA)[:, None],
+            swa[idx.clamp(0, swa.shape[0] - 1)],
+            comp[idx.clamp(0, comp.shape[0] - 1)],
+        )[keep]
+        s = (q[t] @ rows.T) * bmm1_scale
+        m = s.max(dim=1).values
+        if sinks is not None:
+            m = torch.maximum(m, sinks)
+        p = torch.exp(s - m[:, None])
+        denom = p.sum(dim=1)
+        if sinks is not None:
+            denom = denom + torch.exp(sinks - m)
+        out[t] = (p @ rows) / denom[:, None] * bmm2_scale
+    return out
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("width", [128, 200, 384, 512, 640])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tokens", [1, 6, 48])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("with_sinks", [True, False])
+def test_matches_reference(width: int, tokens: int, with_sinks: bool) -> None:
+    c = make_case(tokens, width, seed=width * 1000 + tokens)
+    # The kernel takes only tokens whose clusters are all resident at once,
+    # which depends on the device's SM count (read once the case's tensors
+    # have made the device's context current).
+    tokens = min(tokens, _max_tokens(c["q"].device.index, -(-width // 128)))
+    c.update({key: c[key][:tokens] for key in ("q", "indices", "lens")})
+    sinks = c["sinks"] if with_sinks else None
+    bmm1_scale, bmm2_scale = D**-0.5 * 1.25, 0.75
+    out = torch.full((tokens, H, D), float("nan"), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=DEVICE)
+    args = (c["q"], c["swa_pool"], c["comp_pool"], c["indices"], c["lens"], out)
+    assert supports_sparse_mla_cute(*args, bmm1_scale, bmm2_scale, sinks)
+    sparse_mla_decode(*args, bmm1_scale, bmm2_scale, sinks)
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    ref = reference(c, bmm1_scale, bmm2_scale, sinks)
+    got = out.float()
+    assert not torch.isnan(got).any()
+    torch.testing.assert_close(got, ref, atol=0.03, rtol=0.05)
+    if tokens > 2:
+        assert bool((got[2] == 0).all())
+
+
+def test_cuda_graph_replay_matches_eager() -> None:
+    c = make_case(12, 640, seed=7)
+    args_in = (c["q"], c["swa_pool"], c["comp_pool"], c["indices"], c["lens"])
+    eager = torch.empty((12, H, D), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=DEVICE)
+    sparse_mla_decode(*args_in, eager, D**-0.5, 1.0, c["sinks"])
+    graphed = torch.empty_like(eager)
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        sparse_mla_decode(*args_in, graphed, D**-0.5, 1.0, c["sinks"])
+    graph.replay()
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    assert torch.equal(graphed, eager)
+
+
+def test_declines_unsupported() -> None:
+    c = make_case(4, 640, seed=3)
+    out = torch.empty((4, H, D), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=DEVICE)
+    base = [c["q"], c["swa_pool"], c["comp_pool"], c["indices"], c["lens"], out]
+    assert supports_sparse_mla_cute(*base, 0.1, 1.0, c["sinks"])
+    # Tensor scales, BF16 sinks, a 768-wide set, a BF16 query.
+    assert not supports_sparse_mla_cute(*base, torch.tensor(0.1), 1.0, c["sinks"])
+    assert not supports_sparse_mla_cute(*base, 0.1, 1.0, c["sinks"].bfloat16())
+    wide = torch.zeros((4, 768), dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    assert not supports_sparse_mla_cute(*base[:3], wide, *base[4:], 0.1, 1.0, None)
+    bf16_q = c["q"].bfloat16()
+    assert not supports_sparse_mla_cute(bf16_q, *base[1:], 0.1, 1.0, None)
+    # More tokens than one wave of clusters.
+    many = _max_tokens(torch.accelerator.current_device_index(), 5) + 1
+    big = make_case(many, 640, seed=5)
+    big_out = torch.empty((many, H, D), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=DEVICE)
+    big_args = (
+        big["q"],
+        big["swa_pool"],
+        big["comp_pool"],
+        big["indices"],
+        big["lens"],
+    )
+    assert not supports_sparse_mla_cute(*big_args, big_out, 0.1, 1.0, None)

+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    assert torch.equal(strided, dense)

+"""A TP all-gather over NVLink multicast with a Lamport mailbox, for the
+specialized decode.
+
+The specialized decode gathers small tensors across the TP group on its
+critical path: each dense indexer layer of a row-sharded decode step gathers
+its top-k rows (and the candidate source its candidate blocks), and every step
+gathers the vocab-parallel logits. A few hundred kilobytes at most, so the
+latency of the collective, not its bandwidth, is what counts.
+
+vLLM's custom all-gather has a Lamport kernel for NVLink multicast
+(``mnnvl_lamport_all_gather``), but it never waits for the rank's own
+multicast copy: it takes its own slot from registers, and a copy that lands
+after the next call has cleaned its stage stays there. A later gather of
+another size lays the slots out differently and can read that word as a
+peer's payload. A stress test of back-to-back gathers of alternating sizes in
+CUDA graphs hits this hundreds of times in a few million gathers. This module
+is a gather of the same shape that cannot leave a word behind.
+
+The mailbox is symmetric memory with a multicast mapping, laid out as
+16-byte packs::
+
+    mailbox[generation][rank][pack]    3 generations x TP ranks x capacity
+
+A call runs one kernel, one thread a 16-byte pack of the rank's input:
+
+1. Publish: the thread stores its pack through the multicast address into
+   every rank's ``mailbox[g][rank][pack]``. A word equal to the Lamport
+   sentinel (``0x80000000``: FP32 negative zero, INT32_MIN) goes out as 0.
+2. Collect: it polls ``mailbox[g][r][pack]`` of every rank ``r``, its own
+   included, until no word of it is the sentinel; writes each rank's pack to
+   the output, rank-major as NCCL lays out a dim-0 gather; and stores the
+   sentinel back into the slots it read. Every slot a call writes is read
+   after it has landed and reset by the same call, so no call leaves a word
+   for a later one, whatever the sizes.
+3. Generation: ``state[0]`` is the call's generation. Each CTA reads it once
+   and counts itself in ``state[1]``; the last CTA to arrive advances the
+   generation and clears the count. A rank can be at most one call ahead of
+   a peer (finishing a call needs every rank's payload), so a rank writing
+   the next generation never touches the slots a slower peer still reads;
+   three generations, as vLLM's and FlashInfer's Lamport kernels use, leave
+   one more in between.

+holds the sanitized words on every rank, its own slot included, so all ranks
+see the same bits. The caller must issue calls in the same order on every

+    return llvm.inline_asm(
+        result,
+        operands,
+        text,
+        constraints,
+        has_side_effects=True,
+        is_align_stack=False,
+        asm_dialect=llvm.AsmDialect.AD_ATT,
+        loc=loc,
+        ip=ip,
+    )
+

+    """One 16-byte pack as four words; volatile for the Lamport polls."""
+    opcode = "ld.volatile.global.v4.u32" if volatile else "ld.global.v4.u32"
+    loaded = _asm(
+        llvm.StructType.get_literal([T.i32()] * 4),
+        [address.ir_value(loc=loc, ip=ip)],
+        f"{opcode} {{$0, $1, $2, $3}}, [$4];",
+        "=r,=r,=r,=r,l",
+        loc=loc,
+        ip=ip,
+    )
+    return tuple(
+        Uint32(llvm.extractvalue(T.i32(), loaded, [index], loc=loc, ip=ip))
+        for index in range(4)
+    )
+
+
+@dsl_user_op
+def _store_u32x4(
+    address: Int64,
+    w0: Uint32,
+    w1: Uint32,
+    w2: Uint32,
+    w3: Uint32,
+    multicast: bool,
+    *,
+    loc=None,
+    ip=None,

+    moves the bits unchanged) or to a local one."""

+        "multimem.st.relaxed.sys.global.v4.f32" if multicast else "st.global.v4.u32"
+    )
+    _asm(
+        None,
+        [address.ir_value(loc=loc, ip=ip)]
+        + [word.ir_value(loc=loc, ip=ip) for word in (w0, w1, w2, w3)],
+        f"{opcode} [$0], {{$1, $2, $3, $4}};",
+        "l,r,r,r,r",
+        loc=loc,
+        ip=ip,
+    )

+    return Uint32(
+        _asm(
+            T.i32(),
+            [address.ir_value(loc=loc, ip=ip)],
+            "ld.volatile.global.u32 $0, [$1];",
+            "=r,l",
+            loc=loc,
+            ip=ip,
+        )
+    )

+@dsl_user_op

+    _asm(

+        [address.ir_value(loc=loc, ip=ip), value.ir_value(loc=loc, ip=ip)],
+        "st.global.u32 [$0], $1;",
+        "l,r",
+        loc=loc,
+        ip=ip,
+    )

+class _AllGatherKernel:
+    """One thread a 16-byte pack of the rank's input, ``THREADS`` a CTA."""

+    def __init__(self, rank: int, world_size: int, rank_packs: int) -> None:

+class LamportAllGather:
+    """TP all-gather along dim 0 over NVLink multicast, for inputs of up to
+    ``rank_capacity_bytes`` a rank (a multiple of 16 bytes).
+
+    Construction is collective over the TP group: every rank compiles the
+    kernel and allocates its mailbox, and it raises when NVLink multicast is
+    unavailable. ``accepts`` tells whether a tensor fits, from its size
+    alone, so every rank decides alike.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, *, rank_capacity_bytes: int, device: torch.device) -> None:
+        if rank_capacity_bytes <= 0 or rank_capacity_bytes % PACK_BYTES:
+            raise ValueError("the capacity must be a positive multiple of 16 bytes")
+        group = get_tp_group().device_group
+        self.world_size = world_size = dist.get_world_size(group)
+        rank = dist.get_rank(group)
+        self.rank_capacity_bytes = rank_capacity_bytes
+        rank_packs = rank_capacity_bytes // PACK_BYTES
+        device = torch.device(device)
+        with torch.accelerator.device_index(device.index):
+            # cute.compile returns an untyped JIT executor.
+            self._kernel: Any = cute.compile(
+                _AllGatherKernel(rank, world_size, rank_packs),
+                Int64(0),
+                Int64(0),
+                Int64(0),
+                Int64(0),
+                Int64(0),
+                Int32(1),
+                make_fake_stream(),
+            )
+            self._mailbox = symm_mem.empty(
+                (GENERATIONS * world_size * rank_packs * PACK_BYTES // 4,),
+                dtype=torch.int32,
+                device=device,
+            )
+            self._mailbox_handle = symm_mem.rendezvous(self._mailbox, group)
+            multicast = int(self._mailbox_handle.multicast_ptr or 0)
+            if not multicast or multicast % PACK_BYTES:
+                raise RuntimeError("NVLink multicast mapping is unavailable")
+            self._multicast = multicast
+            # Every slot starts as the sentinel.
+            self._mailbox.fill_(-(2**31))
+            self._state = torch.zeros(2, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+            torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+        dist.barrier(group=group)
+
+    def accepts(self, inp: torch.Tensor) -> bool:
+        """Whether ``inp`` fits: 1 to ``rank_capacity_bytes`` bytes, a
+        multiple of 16."""
+        return 0 < inp.nbytes <= self.rank_capacity_bytes and not inp.nbytes % 16
+
+    def __call__(self, inp: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """Every rank's ``inp`` concatenated along dim 0 in rank order, on the
+        current stream. Words equal to ``0x80000000`` arrive as 0, on every
+        rank (FP32 negative zero becomes positive zero)."""
+        if not self.accepts(inp):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"the all-gather takes 16-byte multiples of up to "
+                f"{self.rank_capacity_bytes} bytes a rank, not {inp.nbytes}"
+            )
+        if not inp.is_contiguous() or inp.data_ptr() % PACK_BYTES:
+            # The kernel loads 16-byte packs.
+            inp = inp.clone(memory_format=torch.contiguous_format)
+        out = torch.empty(
+            (inp.shape[0] * self.world_size, *inp.shape[1:]),
+            dtype=inp.dtype,
+            device=inp.device,
+        )
+        self._kernel(
+            Int64(inp.data_ptr()),
+            Int64(out.data_ptr()),
+            Int64(self._mailbox.data_ptr()),
+            Int64(self._multicast),
+            Int64(self._state.data_ptr()),
+            Int32(inp.nbytes // PACK_BYTES),
+            current_cu_stream(),
+        )
+        return out
